get.summary: Get the authenticated app

post.summary: Create a GitHub App from a manifest
post.desc: Use this endpoint to complete the handshake necessary when implementing the [GitHub App Manifest flow](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/creating-github-apps-from-a-manifest/). When you create a GitHub App with the manifest flow, you receive a temporary `code` used to retrieve the GitHub App's `id`, `pem` (private key), and `webhook_secret`.

get.summary: Get a webhook configuration for an app
get.desc:
Returns the webhook configuration for a GitHub App. For more information about configuring a webhook for your app, see "[Creating a GitHub App](/developers/apps/creating-a-github-app)."

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

patch.summary: Update a webhook configuration for an app
patch.desc:
Updates the webhook configuration for a GitHub App. For more information about configuring a webhook for your app, see "[Creating a GitHub App](/developers/apps/creating-a-github-app)."

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

url.description: The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.

content_type.description: The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include `json` and `form`. The default is `form`.

secret.description: If provided, the `secret` will be used as the `key` to generate the HMAC hex digest value for [delivery signature headers](https://docs.github.com/webhooks/event-payloads/#delivery-headers).

oneOf.description: Determines whether the SSL certificate of the host for `url` will be verified when delivering payloads. Supported values include `0` (verification is performed) and `1` (verification is not performed). The default is `0`. **We strongly recommend not setting this to `1` as you are subject to man-in-the-middle and other attacks.**

get.summary: List deliveries for an app webhook
get.desc:
Returns a list of webhook deliveries for the webhook configured for a GitHub App.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

get.summary: Get a delivery for an app webhook
get.desc:
Returns a delivery for the webhook configured for a GitHub App.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

post.summary: Redeliver a delivery for an app webhook
post.desc:
Redeliver a delivery for the webhook configured for a GitHub App.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

get.summary: List installation requests for the authenticated app
get.desc: Lists all the pending installation requests for the authenticated GitHub App.

get.summary: List installations for the authenticated app
get.desc:
You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.9/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

The permissions the installation has are included under the `permissions` key.

params.name: per_page
params.desc: The number of results per page (max 100).

params.name: page
params.desc: Page number of the results to fetch.

get.summary: Get an installation for the authenticated app
get.desc:
Enables an authenticated GitHub App to find an installation's information using the installation id.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

params.name: installation_id
params.desc: The unique identifier of the installation.

params.desc: The unique identifier of the installation.

get.summary: Get an organization installation for the authenticated app
get.desc:
Enables an authenticated GitHub App to find the organization's installation information.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

params.name: org
params.desc: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

get.summary: Get a repository installation for the authenticated app
get.desc:
Enables an authenticated GitHub App to find the repository's installation information. The installation's account type will be either an organization or a user account, depending which account the repository belongs to.

You must use a [JWT](https://docs.github.com/apps/building-github-apps/authenticating-with-github-apps/#authenticating-as-a-github-app) to access this endpoint.

params.name: owner
params.desc: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

params.name: repo
params.desc: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

put.summary: Add a repository to an app installation
put.desc:
Add a single repository to an installation. The authenticated user must have admin access to the repository.    

This endpoint only works for PATs (classic) with the `repo` scope.

params.name: installation_id
params.desc: The unique identifier of the installation.

params.name: repository_id
params.desc: The unique identifier of the repository.

delete.summary: Remove a repository from an app installation
delete.desc:
Remove a single repository from an installation. The authenticated user must have admin access to the repository. The installation must have the `repository_selection` of `selected`. 

This endpoint only works for PATs (classic) with the `repo` scope.

params.name: installation_id
params.desc: The unique identifier of the installation.

params.name: repository_id
params.desc: The unique identifier of the repository.
